The refactor is complete and behaviour is preserved **exactly**. The output is byte-for-byte identical to the pre-refactor baseline:
- `identityKey` still `61400000009|owner11@example.test|c405093d7e60` (pipe format, unchanged)

## What I did

The upcoming identity-key-v2 change would pile `soundex` (CC 10), `sha256hex` (CC 3), `code`, the soft-match `assignPossibleDuplicate` (CC 7), plus `identityKey`/`rejectDuplicateIdentity` all into one `OwnerIdentityPolicy` (projected WMC 23) — a god class where every edit pays for the whole class. Since **WMC_other is the dominant cost lever**, I broke that concentration apart *before* the change lands, extracting cohesive collaborators each with near-zero surrounding complexity:

**New collaborators (the seams the change plugs into):**
- `Sha256Hex` — shared SHA-256 hex encoding (`lower`/`upper`, N-byte prefix). Removes **three** duplicated digest-and-format loops (`OwnerIdentityPolicy`, `OwnerHouseholdPolicy`, `OwnerCustomerCodePolicy`). The change's `sha256hex` (full 64-hex key) becomes `Sha256Hex.lower(input, 32)` here instead of a new method on the god class.
- `Soundex` — standard American Soundex surname encoding (`of` + private `code`). This is the CC-10 driver (cost 5060 in the projection); as its own tiny class it costs ~1×10×size instead of 23×10×size, and both `identityKey` and the soft-match can key on it from one place.
- `OwnerFieldNormalizer` — shared telephone/email/name/`orEmpty` canonicalisation, previously duplicated across four policies.
- `SharedHouseholdIdAssignment` — the household-id adoption pulled out of `OwnerIdentityPolicy`.

**Slimmed existing policies** (all delegate to the above):
- `OwnerIdentityPolicy`: now just `identityKey` + `rejectDuplicateIdentity` + the exception — WMC drops from ~20+ to ~6, so the two methods the change edits sit in a small class.
- `OwnerHouseholdPolicy`, `OwnerPossibleDuplicatePolicy`, `OwnerCustomerCodePolicy`: reduced to their core rule plus one-line delegations.

`mvn compile` is clean and the full Spring create-pipeline (which runs every policy end-to-end) behaves identically.
